title: Spatiotemporal AI-based modeling of gene regulation and variant effects in the developing human brain using Seal
title_zh: 基于空间时间 AI 的模型：在 Seal 的指导下研究发育中人类大脑的基因调控与变异效应
abstract: Understanding how genetic variation shapes gene regulation in the developing human brain remains a central challenge in neuroscience, particularly in transient cell types and developmental stages where data are limited. We present Seal, an interpretable artificial intelligence (AI) transfer learning framework for genome-based modeling of gene expression and variant effects with spatiotemporal resolution across 26 regions, 30 cell types and 7 developmental stages. Seal predictions provide mechanistic interpretation by linking variants to transcriptional regulators in a spatiotemporal context. Applying Seal to genome-wide association studies, we identify shared and distinct regulatory architectures across six neuropsychiatric conditions that align with clinical trajectories. In the Simons Simplex Collection autism cohort whole-genome data, Seal uncovers a significant burden of de novo regulatory variants in transient fetal excitatory neurons, revealing cell-type-specific and stage-specific effects. By connecting genetic variation to spatiotemporal regulatory programs, Seal offers a general framework for uncovering mechanisms of human brain development and disease.
abstract_zh: 理解遗传变异如何在发育中的人类大脑中塑造基因调控，仍然是神经科学的核心挑战，特别是在数据有限的短暂细胞类型和发育阶段。我们提出了 Seal，一个可解释的转移学习人工智能（AI）框架，用于基于基因组的基因表达和变异效应建模，具备在 26 个区域、30 种细胞类型和 7 个发育阶段的空间时间分辨率。Seal 的预测通过在空间时间背景下将变异链接到转录调控因子，提供机制性解释。将 Seal 应用于基因组关联研究，我们识别出六种精神疾病在监测轨迹上一致的共享与独特的调控架构。在西蒙斯单例自闭症 cohort 的全基因组数据中，Seal 发现了转录性变异在短暂胚胎兴奋性神经元中显著的负担，揭示了细胞类型特异性和阶段特异性效应。通过将遗传变异与空间时间调控程序相连接，Seal 为揭示人类大脑发育和疾病的机制提供了一个通用框架。
